text: The capability area of a data subject request is PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION; recording a request and recording its outcome need the U letter in that area and the list and the view need the R letter; RW-SECADM and RW-PLATADM hold these per TSD P4 v3 T6.1, and RW-COMPLY is granted U in PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION at the matrix load of RWB-P4-E1037-APP so that the role the FSD names as primary can work the request.
why: The legacy permission table, the FSD role table and TSD P4 v3 T6.1 disagree and no source names the capability area or the letter of this feature, so a right has to be fixed before a 403 can be tested; the personal-data screen SCR-47 is an administration screen and the two roles that hold administration letters are the security administrator and the platform administrator.
read: RWB-E8-016 permission checks; FSD P4 v3 A2.27.3.3 and the screen list; TSD P4 v3 T6.1, T6.2 and T3.2 LOV-CAPABILITY; CG-B2-P4-016-3.
confirm: Security administrator and Compliance and PDPA officer
impact: If another capability area or letter is chosen, only the row read by PermissionReader and the 403 fixture change; no schema and no operation changes.

text: The statutory period is the parameter row pd.request.statutory.days with its day-count basis pd.request.statutory.basis and its version label, read through DP-06 from the parameters contract of rwb-case; the due date is the received date plus that period and the version label that fixed it is recorded as the rule version the legacy criterion asks for.
why: NFR-043 leaves the statutory period open at DL26 and gives no number and no basis, and R-UNI-11 names the timer only; a number in code would break BR-P4-027 and the FSD target that a limit change needs no release, so the period has to be data with a version that can be recorded.
read: NFR-043; R-UNI-11; FSD P4 v3 A2.27.3.1 BR-P4-027; DP-06 and the ownership ruling that parameters stay with rwb-case; RWB-E8-016 AC1 ('with the rule version').
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, and the tech lead of rwb-case as the parameter owner
impact: A different row name or owner is a parameter-row change and a contract note within major version 1; if the basis must be working days, only the row value changes and no build is needed.

text: A request has three states in this service, RECEIVED, ANSWERED and REFUSED, and late is a flag derived from completedAt and dueAt and not a fourth state; only a RECEIVED request may take an outcome and an outcome is terminal.
why: No source gives a state set for a data subject request: the legacy story names none, the FSD names a journey of three steps, and the only state machine of the module is the rule package lifecycle of TSD P4 v3 T4, which is another capability's.
read: RWB-E8-016 AC1 and AC2; FSD P4 v3 A2.27.2 and A2.27.4; TSD P4 v3 T4; NFR-043.
impact: An intermediate state such as an open working state would add one operation and one transition, and the contract state set would gain one member within major version 1.

text: The register is scoped by the capability letter and not by case scope, because it holds a case reference and no case attribute; MSG-P4-003, 'This case is not in your scope.', is therefore produced by no operation of this story.
why: The legacy story does not list MSG-P4-003 and the register cannot apply an own, team, region or all scope without reading case data that belongs to rwb-case.
read: RWB-E8-016 validation and messages table; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 default_scope and T6.2; DP-01.
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, and internal audit
impact: If a case scope must apply, the read would need a case attribute through the rwb-case contract and a new C dependency, which the Work Package does not carry.

text: The request-type set, the channel set, the subject-reference shape and the page bounds are parameter rows of rwb-case behind the parameters contract, and the values used in the examples, '30' days at 'PD-2027.1' and '45' at 'PD-2027.2', are synthetic and not business values.
why: The sources give no request-type list, no channel list, no subject-reference shape and no page bounds for this capability, and the contract cannot be tested without a fixed name for each; the values stay with the parameter owner so no business value is written in code.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-case and the data steward
impact: A different row name is a contract note within major version 1; a different set membership is a parameter-row change with no build.

text: The register is the local decision-record chain of the DP-03 library and not a table of rwb-access: the receipt entry carries the request id and the due date, the outcome entry carries the outcome code, the completed time and the late flag, and the four paths and their field sets are fixed by this contract because no source declares them.
why: The ownership map names five tables for P4 and none of them is a request register, and TSD P4 v3 T3.1 has no request table, so the record of a request has to live in the service's own chain rather than in a table invented for the story.
read: Ownership map P4 rows (delegation_limit, masking_rule, permission, role, role_conflict); TSD P4 v3 T3.1; DP-03 and DP-01; FSD P4 v3 A2.27.2 step 3 ('Writes the decision log or interaction ledger entry').
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-access and the decision-record library owner
impact: If a dedicated request table is approved, the app story gains one table and one Flyway step and the contract's field names stay as they are.
